title: Practicing on the prairie and the origin of his big tone
summary: Cobb explains he practiced alone in an open field beside the house, which he feels explains his big Texas tenor tone.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: What I was doing then, Stanley, I was searching, enjoying everybody, admiring everybody, trying to find something for me. I'll tell you what I used to do. You know, I used to practice. Had a prairie on the side of the house where I lived behind the grocery store. (Inaudible) grocery store (inaudible). I used to go out in the prairie where we played ball in the evening and didn't I stand up and blow my horn.
Lot of people asked me, said, where you get that big tone. I said, must have been in the prairie, because I could hear myself ringing all over. But that's where I practiced.
That's interesting because everybody always talks of these big tone Texas tenors, don't they?
I mean most tenor players from Texas do blow with a big tone.
Well, I blew in an open field.
Over from the house where I was living, where what we called the prairie -- we played ball in the evening.
Softball, you know, end up ball, what you call it.
This would account for your big tone. It's like trumpet players who blow outdoors. They develop big tones, don't they? (Inaudible) --
Like if you're blowing out in the open air, and you can hear it ring back even in the open field.

But now, to tell you the truth, I didn't know what I was doing, but I enjoyed it. But I was by myself out there. I didn't worry about nobody coming off -- coming and enjoying me, where in the house I would go disturb somebody, you know, and me learning. Oh, boy, cut that noise out, you know, all this sort of a thing. So I get out there
by myself because, you know, I was sensitive anyway. So I got by myself, and I went in the field.

And it's the same period that I would get out, and I had to scrub the steps and all that on Saturday before I could go out and play ball. I played ball in the same situation. So and that was my life as a kid. And I enjoyed it. I was interested in my horn. I was interested in sports. I wanted to play. I wanted to participate.
